posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
Hi all

Up to now i've only ever used Colorholographic BB plates to make Densiyuk holograms. Sadly I don't have the space or stability required for split beam work. However, i'm quite satisfied with Denisyuk SBR's for the time being.

I fancied having a go with some photopolymer film and note that Sergio sells green sensitive film photopolymer (available in 1m x 20cm samples) at $150.

Has anyone ever used this in a 'Hobby' environment and if so what were the results? Is it suitable for Denisyuk SBR holograms. What problems am I likely to come across if I decide to give this a try? Is it really as easy to process as it sounds (expose to strong white light)?

Perhaps i'm missing something here, but I can't understand why there's so much interest in DCG when Photopolymers seem to provide an ideal solution. Why aren't more people in the hobby sector experimenting with developing photopolymers? I appreciate that DuPont & Co like to keep their formulas a secret and restrict it's use for security holograms, but surely if it's so good more people in the hobby sector would be using it for it's simplicity of processing.

Finally, if I decide to go down the photopolymer route and give Sergio's film a try can I expect to get good, clean and bright SBR holograms using my 100mw Compass 315m?? What exposure times am I likely to need for a piece of film say 10cm square?

Any hints, tips, advice would be much appreciated as i'm a little confused as to why no one else is going down this route.

Cheers

Jem

Thanks for your interest in our products.

Right now, when it comes to display reflection holograms the big issue is bandwidth. We're getting bright monochromatic reconstructions – but at a fairly narrow bandwidth. So under white light image brightness looks rather moderate.

We're definitely working on this and hope to launch a display (broadband) version of our materials soon.

[http://www.polygrama.com](http://www.polygrama.com)

Jem, you said it all, the people on the hobby sector usually need use the film in a Denisyuk simple setup, this is the most difficult requirement for a photopolymer, even our model that bleaches upon exposure due the necessary dye absorption, so the model is more adequate at H2 level with some material tested at photopolymer printing machines in China. (actual sensitivity in green is around ~50mJ/cm², red one is ~3 to 10mJ/cm² index modulation = 0.006 - to be published by one Czech team)

200um is the upper coating thickness limit and we were using ~150um to get results, this is why we are changing the structure a little to ~20um due high costs. However the liquid emulsion did play another league with the first article in the photonics field (Photo - Prague 08) to be published in August, it will release the material into a solid base to be developed since the dry one uses the same principle as SM-TR series.

We are finding our way into scientific community and holographic printing marketing but still aiming the valuable hobby people to simplify the holographer life, however nobody can hurry holography as Jeff said, and we are passing first the science evaluation tests to turn our material a serious promising for the Industry.

I would state that this route is difficult, but rewards are waiting for those with time and money to expend.

posts.author: Sergio
posts.content_md:
Of course John, would be a pleasure. Interesting both 'hobby styled and priced' materials are now the direction for the photopolymer film marketing , the films need to be very practical ( only light/*fast*-heat development), low cost and stable for years, I think for the holographer the polymer will be a choice to test but the first natural choice for the *manufacturer* is security mass production, with optional educational purposes 2nd.

Liquid emulsions is specialized as will be demonstrated with the photonics Czech group using Polygrama SM series, Dupont material even if one day available, would not be practical due the complex heating processing, we plan use some soft UV and a brief 80°C 5 min maximum post exposure and let the air itself do the image enhancement to overmodulation.

posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
Thanks John...

Sergio,

I appreciate there has been a considerable cost in the development of this photopolymer material and the subsequent film. However, I am sorry to say that I feel that the costs of actually getting the film to us here in the UK are creaping a little too high . Sadly it's the postage costs from Brazil and the money transfer costs (on top of the sample cost) that are killing the deal for us. There's also every chance that we would have to pay UK import duty and tax on the package when it arrives in the UK (none of these are your fault I know ). Therefore, much as we want to try the film, Sadly, I think we will have to wait until your European associate has stock available. The actual shipping and payment cost would be less for us at this stage as import from Europe is very reasonable.

I think if we knew that we were going to achieve fantastic results with this film we would perhaps be more inclined to 'have a go'. But being 'pioneers' with commercial products amongst the hobbyist sector can be expensive, and we are able to buy quiet a lot of other materials (with pretty much guaranteed results) for what this is going to cost us to experiment with once all the 'extra' costs are taken into consideration.

Perhaps you can let us know when the material is available in Europe. As John rightly states if this is as good as it sounds there may be great opportunities amongst us hobbyists. Also, the easy availability of photopolymer films to the hobbyist sector could potentially give the hobby a much needed boost 

Thanks

Jem

Our apologies to all the forum members interested in the new Polygrama photopolymers.

At this moment we're overwhelmed by people/companies all over the world, demanding free samples from us. Unfortunately we're a small business only with very limited means. Running this kind of activities, giving out samples for free that is, may become a severe burden on us in the long term.

As soon as our situation improves, we hope to come back to this decision.

Thank you.

Martin & Sergio
